approachQuestion.prompt:
Routes Without Revisits

Given a directed graph, list all simple paths from vertex s to distinct vertex t. A simple path has no repeated vertex. Return each path as its vertex sequence, once, in any order. Stop a path as soon as it reaches t.

Examples:
n=4, outgoing=[[1,2],[2,3],[1,3],[]], s=0,t=3 -> [[0,1,3],[0,1,2,3],[0,2,3],[0,2,1,3]].
n=2, outgoing=[[],[]], s=0,t=1 -> [].

Constraints: 2 <= n <= 12; no repeated directed edges or self loops; adjacency lists are supplied. Cycles are allowed. 0 <= s,t < n and s!=t.

options.text: Explore every outgoing edge to a vertex not on the current path, undoing that vertex’s mark on return. Copy paths at t and stop extending them.
options.feedback: A repeated vertex is forbidden within one path, but another path may use it. Branch-local membership prevents cycles without suppressing alternative routes.

options.text: Permanently mark a vertex after its first visit, as in a reachability search.
options.feedback: In the first example, reaching vertex 2 through 1 would prevent later exploring the distinct path [0,2,3].

options.text: Do not track path membership; instead cap every attempted path at n vertices and emit any path reaching t within that cap.
options.feedback: For n=5, outgoing=[[1],[0,4],[],[],[]], s=0,t=4, this accepts [0,1,0,1,4]: its five vertices fit the cap, but vertices 0 and 1 repeat.

options.text: Carry a fresh copied n-entry membership array in every child call instead of applying and undoing one mark.
options.feedback: This is correct but copies the full vertex state for every branch; reversible single-entry updates avoid that extra work.

feedback.reason: A repeated vertex is forbidden within one path, but another path may use it. Branch-local membership prevents cycles without suppressing alternative routes.
details: Allocate n path-membership flags and mark s. At a nonterminal call scan outgoing neighbors, recurse only on unmarked vertices after appending and marking them, then undo both changes. At t copy the current path and return without scanning its outgoing edges.

Visited flags mean membership in the current route, not permanent discovery. Unmark on return so another simple route may reuse the vertex. At t emit and stop that branch rather than extending beyond the destination.

“Explore every outgoing edge to a vertex not on the current path, undoing that vertex’s mark on return. Copy paths at t and stop extending them.”: A repeated vertex is forbidden within one path, but another path may use it. Branch-local membership prevents cycles without suppressing alternative routes.
“Permanently mark a vertex after its first visit, as in a reachability search.”: In the first example, reaching vertex 2 through 1 would prevent later exploring the distinct path [0,2,3].

“Do not track path membership; instead cap every attempted path at n vertices and emit any path reaching t within that cap.”: For n=5, outgoing=[[1],[0,4],[],[],[]], s=0,t=4, this accepts [0,1,0,1,4]: its five vertices fit the cap, but vertices 0 and 1 repeat.

“Carry a fresh copied n-entry membership array in every child call instead of applying and undoing one mark.”: This is correct but copies the full vertex state for every branch; reversible single-entry updates avoid that extra work.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-17-search` only. Let V count calls, E count outgoing-list entries scanned across all nonterminal calls, and R count vertex IDs copied into returned paths. Initialize n flags; each append/mark/undo is constant amortized work. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n + V + E + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n+m+R) time, O(n) auxiliary space, with m the graph edge count
O(n + V + E + R) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(n + V + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Count actual path-state edge scans; a vertex may be revisited on different routes.
details: Flags initialize in n work; calls contribute V and adjacency scanning E, with result copying R. A vertex’s adjacency list may be scanned on many different paths.
An n-entry membership array and one path/stack of length at most n are retained.

Let V count calls, E count outgoing-list entries scanned across all nonterminal calls, and R count vertex IDs copied into returned paths. Initialize n flags; each append/mark/undo is constant amortized work.
“O(n+m+R) time, O(n) auxiliary space, with m the graph edge count”: An edge may be scanned repeatedly for different path prefixes.
“O(n + V + E + R) time, O(V) auxiliary space”: The full call tree is not stored.
“O(n + V + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Neighbor entries rejected by membership checks still cost scan work.
